name: Cervan
traits: Medium deerlike humanoid. Walking speed 30 ft. Constitution +2. Proficiency in one of Athletics, Medicine, Nature, or Survival.

Surge of Vigor. When an attack inflicts more than half your current HP in damage, immediately regain 1d12 + your Constitution modifier HP. This can trigger when the hit takes you to 0 HP. Once per long rest.
Grove cervan. Dexterity +1 and walking speed 35 ft. Long jump 30 ft. and high jump 15 ft. with or without a running start. Opportunity attacks against you have disadvantage.

Pronghorn cervan. Strength +1. Double carrying capacity and push, drag, and lift limits. Antler unarmed strike deals 1d6 + Strength modifier piercing. After moving at least 20 ft. straight toward an opponent, the charge costs a bonus action and adds 1d6 piercing. A Large or smaller target makes a Strength save at DC 8 + proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier. On failure, push it 10 ft. away into a space you choose.
Speak, read, and write Birdfolk. Cervan is spoken only.

name: Hedge
traits: Small hedgehoglike humanoid. Walking speed 25 ft., burrowing speed 15 ft. through soil. Charisma +2, Wisdom +1.
Spiny Quills. Armor cannot be worn. Base AC is 14 + Dexterity modifier. A shield still grants its bonus if proficient.

Curl Up. As an action, curl into a ball. Base AC becomes 19 without a Dexterity bonus, and a usable shield still applies. While curled, you cannot move, attack, or cast spells that have a somatic component. A creature that misses you with a melee attack takes 2d4 piercing. If a creature hits you, you fall prone at the end of the turn. You may uncurl during your turn.
Forest Magic. Know druidcraft and cast animal messenger at 2nd level once per short or long rest. Both use Charisma.
Speak With Bugs. Convey simple ideas to Beast insects, spiders, worms, and similar creatures using sounds and gestures. Speak, read, and write Birdfolk and Hedge.

name: Jerbeen
traits: Small mouse- or jerboa-like humanoid. Walking speed 30 ft. Dexterity +2, Charisma +1. Standing long jump 30 ft. and high jump 15 ft., with or without a running start.
Nimbleness. Move through a larger creature’s space. Team Tactics allows the Help action as a bonus action.

Take Heart. Gain advantage on Strength saves and on saves against being frightened when you are within 5 ft. of an ally you can see and hear, provided that ally is neither frightened nor incapacitated.
Speak, read, and write Birdfolk and Jerbeen.

name: Mapach
traits: Medium raccoonlike humanoid. Walking speed 30 ft., climb speed 20 ft., darkvision 60 ft. Wisdom +2, Constitution +1.
Resilience. Advantage on saving throws against poison and resistance to poison damage. Skulker grants advantage on Stealth checks in dim light or darkness.

Scroungecraft. Gain tinker’s tools proficiency. With suitable material, spend 10 minutes to improvise a tool or piece of adventuring gear worth up to 30 gp. Tools and expendable items are useful for one use. Other items generally last 1 hour.

With proper materials, start before the temporary item fails and spend 8 hours to make it permanent. Scroungecraft can also repair equipment, with available materials and repair durability at the GM’s discretion.
Speak, read, and write Birdfolk and Mapach.

name: Vulpin
traits: Medium foxlike humanoid. Walking speed 30 ft., darkvision 60 ft. Intelligence +2, Charisma +1.
Bite. Use Strength or Dexterity for both attack and damage rolls for this unarmed strike. Damage is 1d6 piercing plus the chosen modifier.
Evasive. Add your Intelligence modifier to Dexterity saving throws.

Bewitching Guile. Cast charm person at first level, ambush prey at third level as a 2nd-level spell, and fear at fifth level. Each racial spell has its own use per long rest. These spells use Intelligence.

Ambush prey. Become invisible for up to 1 hour. Moving at least 5 ft. from the casting point ends it. The first attack against an unaware target deals an extra 1d6 damage and ends the effect. Full spell rules are on p. 49.
Speak, read, and write Birdfolk and Vulpin.
